methodological_questions: how to quantify offensive reorganization relative to L
how to estimate causal effect of reorganization on points per possession
how to control for confounding factors
whether sample size is sufficient for adequate power

historical_evidence.finding: Connector absence displaces team offensive identity (D_A) more than usage-matched non‑organizer absence; unmatched conn vs role D_A 0.2020 vs 0.1021, t=5.97 p=2.87e-08; usage‑matched vs role paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, t=6.35 p=7.35e-09 n=96.

failed_approaches.why: n is small for most players (single‑game playsheets); no multiplicity or clustered test.
Labeled similarity does not separate absorption from cascade; almost always findable.

evidence_establishes: Connector absence causes measurable shift in offensive identity (D_A) relative to usage‑matched controls.
evidence_does_not_establish: The magnitude of this identity shift predicts changes in points per possession; no study has linked D_A changes to PPP outcomes.
own_inferences: Offensive reorganization can be operationalized via changes in play‑type distribution or offensive identity metrics (e.g., D_A). A causal test requires comparing PPP before and after player absence while controlling for team, opponent, game context, and prior performance.
uncertainties: Exact definition of “reorganization relative to L” is unclear; how to measure L; whether existing data capture all necessary covariates; true variance of the reorganization metric across teams and seasons.

historical_effect.explanation: Historical studies have not addressed the specific relationship between reorganization and PPP, so the decision to proceed relies on internal evaluation of feasibility rather than past results.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 986 units (spells) across 5 seasons; limited power for detecting small PPP effects
Reliability of reorganization metric (e.g., D_A) depends on accurate play‑type labeling and sufficient possessions per spell
Potential confounding by opponent defense, game tempo, and player usage changes

prior_work.summary: Prior work has quantified the effect of connector absence on offensive identity but not linked that identity shift to points‑per‑possession outcomes.

risks.text: Limited number of spells reduces ability to detect modest PPP changes
Reorganization metric may be noisy if derived from sparse possession data
Unobserved team or opponent factors may bias PPP changes

design.estimand: Effect of change in offensive reorganization (ΔD_A) on change in points per possession (ΔPPP) for spells with a player absence versus matched control spells
design.unit: team‑spells (e.g., 5‑minute segments before and after absence)
design.sample: All spells from 2022‑23 through 2025‑26 playoffs with ≥30 possessions pre‑ and post‑absence; matched on team, opponent, game stage, and pre‑absence PPP
design.power: Target α=0.05, power=0.80 for detecting a 0.05 PPP increase; requires ~200 matched pairs (currently ~96, so additional seasons or relaxed matching criteria recommended)
design.controls: Fixed effects for team, opponent, game period; include pre‑absence PPP, tempo, and player usage; use difference‑in‑differences framework
design.falsification: Test on spells where no player absence occurred but with similar pre‑absence PPP to confirm no systematic PPP drift
design.multiplicity: Pre‑define primary test; secondary tests for subgroups (e.g., starters vs bench) with Bonferroni correction
design.decision_rule: Reject null if |β|>critical value; report confidence intervals; if power insufficient, stop study
design.data_version: Per‑game play‑by‑play and possession graph database up to 2025‑26 playoffs (complete)
